newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan needs to sell JR shares early - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan needs to sell JR shares early - MOF.

text.p: The government needs to sell state-owned shares left in JR Group companies, which formerly made up the state-owned Japanese National Railways (JNR), as soon as possible, a senior Finance Ministry official told a parliamentary committee on Tuesday.

JNR Settlement Corp, the state-owned agent in charge of settling the debt and assets left by JNR after it was split into seven Japan Railways Group (JR) companies in 1987, still holds shares in the group companies.
"The shares held by JNR Settlement Corp must be disposed of as soon as possible," the official said.
The government sold some of its shares in the two biggest firms in the JR group -- East Japan Railway Co and West Japan Railway Co -- when the companies were listed on stock exchanges.
On Monday, a senior executive of unlisted Shikoku Railway Co, a JR Group firm, told reporters the company wants to list shares as early as fiscal 2001/02.
Other unlisted group firms Kyushu Railway Co and Hokkaido Railway Co have already announced similar listing targets.
